title: Understanding Australia's Minimum Wage: How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay
description: Learn how to convert hourly pay to annual salary using australia's minimum wage as a guide. Includes tax, Medicare, super, and fortnightly calculations for 38-hour weeks.
salarySummary: For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, annual gross pay is your hourly rate multiplied by 1,976 hours (38 × 52).

faqs.q: How is annual salary calculated from an hourly rate in Australia?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52 weeks. For a standard 38-hour week, use 38 × 52 = 1,976 hours. This gives gross annual pay before tax and super.

faqs.q: Does the National Minimum Wage include casual loading?
faqs.a: No. The National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour (from 1 July 2026) is for permanent employees. Casual employees receive an additional 25% loading, making the minimum casual rate $33.05 per hour. Super is paid on top of the base rate.

faqs.q: How is tax and Medicare calculated on annual income?
faqs.a: For 2026-27, resident tax rates apply: nil up to $18,200, then 15% to $45,000, 30% to $135,000, 37% to $190,000, and 45% above. Medicare levy is 2% (using 2025-26 thresholds for singles). Super guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top, up to the maximum contribution base.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Hourly Pay to Annual Salary

Whether you are negotiating a job offer, comparing roles, or simply planning your finances, knowing how to convert an hourly rate to an annual figure is essential. In Australia, the standard full-time week is 38 hours, and the formula is straightforward: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52**. This gives your gross annual pay before tax, Medicare, and superannuation.

For example, using **australia's minimum wage** of $26.44 per hour (from 1 July 2026), a full-time employee working 38 hours each week earns:

$26.44 × 38 × 52 = **$52,254.88 per year**.

If you are paid fortnightly, simply multiply your weekly gross by two. For the minimum wage, that is $1,004.90 per week, or **$2,009.80 per fortnight**.

### What If You Work Different Hours?

The formula works for any weekly hours. If you work 20 hours per week, your annual gross is $26.44 × 20 × 52 = $27,497.60. Always use your actual agreed hours. The [the timesheet](/) on this site lets you enter your base hourly rate and automatically calculates annual, monthly, fortnightly, and weekly figures.

## Understanding Australia's Minimum Wage

The National Minimum Wage is set by the Fair Work Commission and applies to employees not covered by an award or agreement. As of 1 July 2026, it is **$26.44 per hour** for permanent employees. This is the legal floor – most workers are entitled to more under their industry award or enterprise agreement.

### Award Rates and Casual Loading

Many industries have specific award rates that are higher than the minimum. For example, the hospitality or retail awards often set higher minimums for certain classifications. Casual employees receive an additional **25% loading** on top of the base rate to compensate for lack of paid leave. The casual minimum wage is therefore $33.05 per hour ($26.44 × 1.25).

**Important:** When using a calculator, never enter a rate that already includes casual loading. Instead, enter the base hourly rate and select the casual loading option – the tool will add the 25% for you. See our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page for more details.

### Superannuation Is Paid on Top

Employers must pay super guarantee at **12% of ordinary earnings** (from 1 July 2026) on top of your gross pay. This is not deducted from your hourly rate. For a minimum-wage full-time worker, super adds $6,270.59 per year ($52,254.88 × 0.12), up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

## Tax and Medicare on Your Annual Pay

Once you have your gross annual figure, the Australian Taxation Office applies progressive tax rates. For the 2026-27 income year, the resident tax brackets are:

- $0 – $18,200: **nil**
- $18,201 – $45,000: **15%** on the excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: **30%** on the excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: **37%** on the excess over $135,000
- $190,001 and above: **45%** on the excess over $190,000

In addition, the **Medicare levy** is generally **2%** of your taxable income. The 2025-26 single reduction thresholds (used here because the 2026-27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of preparation) mean that low-income earners may pay a reduced rate or nil.

### Example: Minimum Wage Tax Calculation

For a full-time worker earning $52,254.88:

- Tax-free threshold: $18,200 → taxable income $34,054.88
- Tax on first bracket ($18,201–$45,000): 15% of $26,800 = $4,020
- Tax on next bracket ($45,001–$52,254.88): 30% of $7,254.88 = $2,176.46
- Total tax: $6,196.46
- Medicare levy (2% of $52,254.88): $1,045.10
- Total tax and Medicare: **$7,241.56**

Your after-tax annual pay would be approximately $45,013.32, or **$865.64 per week** ($1,731.28 per fortnight).

For a more precise estimate tailored to your situation, use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool.

## Using the Timesheet and Reference Tables

Our [the timesheet](/) is designed for quick conversions. Enter your base hourly rate, select your hours per week (default 38), and optionally check the casual loading box. The tool shows your annual, monthly, fortnightly, and weekly gross pay, plus estimated tax, Medicare, and super.

For award rates and industry averages, refer to our [pay guides](/blog) and [reference tables](/data). The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports that full-time adult ordinary time earnings averaged $2,083.70 per week in May 2026 – that is about **$108,352 per year** for a 38-hour week. Remember, this is an average across all industries, not a median for your specific job. See [average pay](/topics/average-pay) for more context.

## Important Notes and Disclaimer

The calculations on this page assume:
- The same hourly rate every week, with no unpaid overtime
- No penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice
- Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base
- Tax uses the 2026-27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold
- Medicare uses the 2025-26 single reduction thresholds (the 2026-27 thresholds were not confirmed)
- HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted

This is an **estimate**, not a determination of your pay or tax liability. Always consult a qualified professional or the Fair Work Ombudsman for your specific circumstances.
